key_insight: Verdict stability did not reliably distinguish diagnoses based on real medical images from those produced with blank placeholders.
clinical_relevance: A medical vision–language model’s persistence or apparent certainty should not be treated as evidence that it used the diagnostic image.
method: Evaluated 60 Italian State Examination items with real images versus blank placeholders.
Applied contentless doubt (L1) or fabricated consensus (L4) as adversarial pressure.
Compared paired verdict reversals and answer changes over ten turns.
evidence_signal: Fabricated consensus overturned 94.4% of real-image verdicts versus 98.1% with blank images; contentless doubt overturned 62.5% versus 51.8%, respectively.
watch_item: Findings from this model evaluation on 60 examination items require validation across other models and clinical datasets before broader generalization.
paper_title: Conviction Without Evidence: Verdict Stability Is Independent of Visual Grounding in Medical Vision--Language Models
